4b1d97465d07c357444af14e4a5fb856d0437371.summary: This is a GitHub repository README for Tactical RMM, an open-source remote monitoring and management tool built with Django, Vue and Go, with a golang agent that integrates with MeshCentral. It lists product features such as remote desktop, a real-time remote shell, file browsing, patch management, and automated alerting, plus supported Windows, Linux and Mac agent versions. It describes a software product and does not report a threat, actor, campaign, malware or vulnerability.

4b7c4cbaa216abc9ffac4ec57b0fa54b7d2672a8.summary: eSentire's Threat Response Unit reports Russian-speaking affiliates of the ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware gang using Google ads to lure users to attacker-controlled sites. Victims download the Nitrogen initial-access malware, which uses obfuscated Python libraries and leads to ALPHV/BlackCat ransomware. The report says the unit stopped attempts against a law firm, a manufacturer and a warehouse provider in its customers' networks. It also recounts ALPHV/BlackCat's history and victims, including MGM Resorts and McClaren Health Care, and notes browser-based access as a growing route into ransomware…

4bcaa0ea749e55f9e9d29669df670aa5c4f7e569.summary: A guide signed airwalk on placing backdoors and trojan horses in Unix systems and detecting them. It recalls historical cases such as Crackerjack, SATAN, quota, ircII and a Slackware account backdoor, describes common backdoor and trojan techniques in general terms, and presents Tripwire as an integrity-checking defence. It is instructional rather than a report on a specific campaign.

hedges: The report says its list of historical cases is not complete: these aren't all examples of backdoors and trojan horses on Unix systems.
The report says backdoors cannot be generalized and that the best technique depends on the system being targeted.
The report says its simple detection scripts are quite primitive and not so reliable, and that a perfect system cannot exist.
The report says the telnet trojan only guesses the host's system type, so it is not good against smart users.
The report says the SUID shell check is not a full-proof technique and that protection against backdoors is weak.
